2.text: fish-roe forms one of the important items in the diet of the inhabitants, and

3.text: is used, mixed with flour, for baking a special kind of cakes. Moreover, the

4.text: fish come into the rivers full of roe for the purpose of spawning. To catch

5.text: no spawning fish is to catch almost nothing. The next year the same official

6.text: ordered the Russian creoles of the Lower Kolyma to undertake another

7.text: experiment, that of making salt. A party was sent to the seashore. They

8.text: took with them a large kettle, gathered some fuel, and tried to extract the

9.text: salt from the water by boiling it. All these experiments, too, were undertaken

10.text: in the summer-time, when every pair of working hands and every hour of

11.text: time are of exceeding value to the population.

12.text: Two years before that the Governor of Yakutsk also was possessed by

13.text: the idea of reforms. So he ordered the chief officer of Kolymsk to exterminate

14.text: immediately all the team-dogs of the Kolyma country, and to replace them

15.text: with driving-reindeer. Each house-master had to receive five reindeer. The

16.text: order says, “The dogs consume the food of men. Therefore famine comes

17.text: so often.” This order, however, was not put into execution. Otherwise the
17.note: closing quote after 'often.' is curly U+201D CLOSE DOUBLE QUOTATION MARK; machine draft had a straight quote here.

18.text: whole fishing population of the Kolyma River, Russian, Yakut, and Yukaghir,

19.text: who know nothing about reindeer-breeding, would be left “walking,” as they

20.text: say on the Kolyma. It is needless to add that this population literally could

21.text: not exist without their dog-teams. Reforms of this kind have not ceased up

22.text: to the present time. Thus I was informed that in the year 1906 a new one

23.text: was undertaken. In this year, after the well-known revolutionary outbreaks,

24.text: an order was issued in St. Petersburg for the confiscation of arms throughout

25.text: the country. This order duly reached the Kolyma. Then the assessor of

26.text: the district went up the river, taking the firelocks from the Tungus hunters,

27.text: and even the belt-knives¹ from the whole sedentary population.
27.note: Footnote marker after 'belt-knives' is superscript U+00B9, matching the note opener on line 41. The machine draft misread the raised sort as an exclamation mark ('belt-knives !').

28.text: Relief of Famine. — It is at least the duty of an Administration that

29.text: costs so much, both to the state and to the population, to assist the people

30.text: in times of public calamities, which in these countries occur almost yearly as

31.text: regularly as the seasons change. The Administration has to lend assistance

32.text: in times of famine, and to afford medical succor in times of disease. Only those

33.text: that pay tribute have a right to this official assistance. Famines occur on

34.text: the Kolyma at least every other year. Their usual season is during the months

35.text: of March and April, when all the stored provisions are exhausted, and fresh

36.text: supplies have not yet come to hand. To relieve famine, the Administration

37.text: has arranged for the collection of supplies of dried and frozen fish. Each

38.text: community has its separate stores, and the members of some are obliged to

39.text: turn over yearly one tenth, and even one seventh, of the whole product of

40.text: their fisheries. Accordingly the stores must increase from year to year in
